transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My thoughts won’t slow down, and it’s gotten to the point where I can’t focus enough to do my work safely. I'm an apprentice pipefitter, and I'm just really overwhelmed because I can't keep my head straight on the job site right now.
Have you struggled with these difficulties in focusing and restlessness since you were a child, or is this a recent change that has developed over the past few months?

No, this isn't something from when I was a kid; it's definitely a recent change. All of this trouble with my focus, restlessness, and mood swings really started over the last five to nine months, right after our crew got assigned to a big project in downtown Miami.

Over these past few months, have you felt a persistent loss of interest or pleasure in the activities you usually enjoy, or do you find that your mood is primarily dominated by constant worry and tension?

It’s definitely more of a heavy lack of interest and apathy rather than just constant worry. I used to be obsessed with learning new tricks on the welding torch and helping kids at the community center, but lately I just stare at my tools or my phone for hours and can't bring myself to care enough to show up.
Have you experienced any similar periods of feeling this low, apathetic, or unable to function in the past, perhaps several years ago or before this current project started?

No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. These heavy feelings and not being able to function only started during this current project in Miami. Before this, I was always able to handle my work and stay on top of things.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or appetite since you started feeling this way?

My sleep has been completely thrown off—some nights I lie awake wired until 3 or 4 AM with my brain buzzing, while other times I crash for 12 hours straight and still wake up exhausted. I haven't really noticed any major changes in my appetite, though.
During those nights when your brain is buzzing and you stay awake until 3 or 4 AM, do you feel an unusual surge of energy, increased confidence, or a need to talk more than usual?

Yes, absolutely—I get this massive surge of energy where I feel like I have to do ten things at once, like reorganizing my apartment or signing up for certifications at midnight. My confidence shoots way up too, and I honestly feel like I'm the only one who can redesign the whole Miami water system. When I get going like that, I talk constantly and so fast about my ideas that people have to cut me off because I just can't stop.

During these periods where you feel high energy and extreme confidence, how many days in a row do these symptoms typically last, and have they ever caused you to get into serious trouble or require hospitalization?

These high-energy periods usually last for weeks at a time, as part of a rollercoaster that's been going on for about five months. I've never been hospitalized, but it has caused serious trouble at work. My foreman gave me a formal warning for being unsafe and erratic, and I eventually had to step back from my apprenticeship.

During these past five months, do you experience these periods of high energy and grandiosity as distinct 'high' phases that alternate with your 'low' periods, or are you experiencing symptoms of both high energy and low mood at the same time?

They definitely feel like distinct phases on a rollercoaster rather than happening at the same time. I'll have these high stretches where I'm on top of the world and feel like I can redesign the whole Miami water system, and then I'll crash into a low period where I feel heavy, guilty, and completely drained. Even though my mood can swing quickly, they still feel like separate up and down phases.
During your most recent low period, did you experience any moments where you felt so hopeless or empty that you considered harming yourself?

Yes, on the worst days I lie there before work thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. I've even caught myself looking at my pill bottles and planning out how many it would take, which scared me enough to call off and stay with my mom.

During those high-energy periods, have you ever engaged in risky behaviors—such as spending excessive amounts of money, reckless driving, or other impulsive actions—that resulted in significant, long-lasting consequences for your life or safety?

I haven't really done things like reckless driving or wild spending sprees. But I have done some slightly unsafe things, like taking selfies on a high scaffold at two in the morning when I was feeling on top of the world.

During those high-energy periods, did your symptoms ever become so severe that they caused a marked impairment in your social or occupational functioning, or were they mild enough that you were still able to function reasonably well?

They absolutely caused severe impairment, not mild. I actually had to step back from my pipefitting apprenticeship because my foreman said I wasn't safe or reliable on the job site anymore. I've also completely drifted away from my friends and the community center because I just can't keep up with plans or trust my mood enough to show up.
